title: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) - n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Pierre Dubois

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) filter targeting n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on 128° YX LiNbO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 4140.1 MHz and bandwidth of 359.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: 128° YX LiNbO3
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: Ansys HFSS 2024R1
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design targeting n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4140.1 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       359.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.2 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 17.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 22.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 27.0 dB
Q Factor:               1661
Temperature Coefficient:-21.8 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.2 x 2.0 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   7
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Ansys HFSS 2024R1 and load the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 128° YX LiNbO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4140.1 MHz, BW 359.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.2 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, 128° YX LiNbO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 12420 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.2 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 17.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 540 MHz offset >= 22.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 8 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 11.3 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +25 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 98%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-09-02
Devices Tested:         65
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.94 dB
Return Loss (meas):     18.7 dB
Rejection (meas):       25.4 dB
Isolation (meas):       32.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        1661
Group Delay Variation:  3.5 ns
Power Handling:         +26 dBm
Die Yield:              95.9%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated below-target performance for n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Rejection at near-band offset requires additional resonator tuning.
d) Slight frequency drift observed at +85°C; TC layer thickness may need adjustment.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
